measured_unit_costs_for_this_market.basis: the committed cross-run paid ledger's own 181 Indianapolis attempts, not an estimate
measured_unit_costs_for_this_market.note: the market's own firecrawl average (0.1005 USD) runs above the cross-market measured rate (0.0721) because this market's attempts skew to the harder brands; the cost plan uses the cross-market rate, so the request is if anything understated and the cap should be enforced on ATTEMPTS

firecrawl.hard_cap_recommended: 36 attempts / 25 credits -- a ceiling on attempts, not on the balance

bright_data.why: 128 Bright Data attempts are already on record for this market (100 browser + 28 web unlocker). The rows this revalidation could not settle are the same Marriott, Hilton and Hyatt surfaces those attempts already returned UNEXPECTED_PAGE, IDENTITY_MISMATCH or ACCESS_DENIED on. Firecrawl is the untried rung and is cheaper; Bright Data should not be re-bought until Firecrawl has answered.

google_places.why: 143 Google Places discovery attempts are already committed for this market and 96 of the 100 unrouted rows are among them. Ninety-one came back UNBOUND_NO_SANCTIONED_KEY: Places answered, and the answer was that it has no sanctioned URL for that row. Re-running them would pay a second time to FIND a page, which the standing rule forbids. Only 4 rows are a genuinely new question.

phase_14_paid_readiness.the_honest_headline: Indianapolis coverage expansion is NOT cheap. The 100 rows with no official URL look like an opportunity and are mostly a closed question: paid discovery has already been run against 96 of them. The remaining real yield in this market is the 36-row Firecrawl policy cohort at roughly 2.60 USD, plus attended reads for the Choice and Motel 6 surfaces that time out rather than refuse.

phase_18_regression.why_a_full_run_was_owed: three of this order's five new artifacts (the shadow policy evidence, the pending application inventory and the firecrawl cost plan) match no PATH_RULES entry and classify UNCLASSIFIED. The classifier's rule is that an unclaimed path costs the full suite, and regression_delta.py states in its own comments that the rest of launch_packages/pettripfinder deliberately stays UNCLASSIFIED and that this is 'not an oversight to be tidied up with a blanket rule'. Adding a rule, or renaming these files to match an existing narrow glob, would have been gaming the gate rather than passing it. The matrix was obeyed.

proved_by_identity_not_by_count.rule: a matching failure COUNT proves nothing; the failing sets must be the same set

collection_delta_explained.why_it_is_not_a_regression: the f75aa95 baseline was taken in a fresh worktree with no untracked data corpora; this worktree collects 87 more parametrised cases from the data present here. All 87 passed -- the failing set is identical node id for node id, so the extra collection adds coverage and no failure.

second_commit_delta_scoped.why: it changes one *_report_*.json and nothing else, which is a narrow class the matrix already names -- exactly the case the V2 delta classifier exists to make cheap
